pr_title: Fix #26849 by adding the domain of the current SSO provider to the form-action CSP
pr_body:
Fixes #26849

Without the SSO provider in form-action CSP, a browser will reject the redirect to the SSO provider after clicking on the 'Login or Register' button introduced by #26083.

The CSP header on instances not using a single SSO method as their sole authentication method should remain unaltered.
pr_comments: Just subscribed this PR, looking forward to the progress of approving it so that I can change my env back.
@CSDUMMI Hi is it possible that you can request someone to review the changes of it? Thanks!

> I wonder if it's the correct approach, I'm a bit uneasy with broadening the CSP here, as an attacker could perform `POST` queries against the SSO provider.

What could be done, at least for the OpenID Connect protocol, is to access the precise URI on the SSO provider, where a user is redirected to. An attacker could then only make POST requests to that precise URI - which ought to have little sensitive information for them - providing either a login form or a redirect back to mastodon.

I'm looking into how to do this for OIDC and then I'll see whether / how this can be done for SAML and CAS.

Hi guys, I just started to wonder if a one-click log in is necessary for us who have set OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true.
Can't we just use the old log in page with only one log in button? I do not mind that honestly... I went through all PRs related to this function and I can see it is causing some problems. @ClearlyClaire could you please tell me what do you think?

I do not mind that honestly... I went through all PRs related to this function and I can see it is causing some problems. @ClearlyClaire could you please tell me what do you think?

By introducing this, Mastodon has made it more convenient and less confusing to use an external identity provider with OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true. The `/auth/sign_in` page on instance with this setup is pointless and thus can confuse users when first encountering it & waste their time thereafter every time they login.

The `/auth/sign_in` page on instance with this setup is pointless and thus can confuse users when first encountering it & waste their time thereafter every time they login.

Got it, make sense, thanks for the explanation

> I just started to wonder if a one-click log in is necessary for us who have set OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true.
> Can't we just use the old log in page with only one log in button?

I'd honestly be fine with that, the one-click flow requires widening the security exceptions a little more than I'd like.

To reduce those security exceptions, I'm now using the exact URI that CAS, SAML and OpenID redirect to.
Any attacker can thus only create forms that go to that exact URI and nowhere else on the IdP.

> To reduce those security exceptions, I'm now using the exact URI that CAS, SAML and OpenID redirect to. Any attacker can thus only create forms that go to that exact URI and nowhere else on the IdP.

Unfortunately, you cannot use paths/full URIs in Content-Security-Policy values

> > To reduce those security exceptions, I'm now using the exact URI that CAS, SAML and OpenID redirect to. Any attacker can thus only create forms that go to that exact URI and nowhere else on the IdP.
> 
> Unfortunately, you cannot use paths/full URIs in Content-Security-Policy values


Are you sure about that? According to [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/Sources#sources) a host-source can contain a scheme, host, port and path.

> > > To reduce those security exceptions, I'm now using the exact URI that CAS, SAML and OpenID redirect to. Any attacker can thus only create forms that go to that exact URI and nowhere else on the IdP.

Oh, you appear to be right! Not sure why I thought otherwise!

This sounds like a good idea in theory, but I'm afraid this would cause the Mastodon server to fail starting if the OIDC provider is momentarily down.
I have added the `ONE_CLICK_SSO_LOGIN` environment variable. If this is set to true, the one-click login is enabled and the CSP policy is also set.

This is getting better, thanks!

In the meantime, I've been investigating how to *tighten* `form-action` and came up with https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/26897

To avoid crashes at start, we may want to use a lambda and rescue any OIDC discovery error (but only cache the result when there is no error)

I'm wondering whether, in this setup, having Mastodon silently fail when the IdP is down is actually wanted. 

Given that we are only talking about a scenario, where all authentication has to go through the IdP, that IdP being down will severely impact Mastodon users. They will see a 502 error when trying to  login & logout.

So, perhaps having the startup fail is actually what we want to happen in this case, with the ability to circumvent the failure (knowingly, instead of silently) using `ONE_CLICK_SSO_LOGIN=false`.

I think transient failures preventing Mastodon from starting up may be an issue, yes, for instance in cases the IDP and Mastodon or on the same network and it is recovering from a power failure, Mastodon failing to start because the IDP hasn't started yet could be an issue.

In any case, I'm ok with the fail-at-startup as long as it is behind a documented switch, so I'm fine with this PR as is (except for it missing `app/controllers/concerns/web_app_controller_concern.rb`)

issue_context.title: When OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true the web interface stuck and cannot log in v4.2.0
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Use the latest nightly docker image
2. In the env, set `OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true` because I am using OIDC login and it works well
3. Run `docker compose up -d` and you will see that you stuck on the page you are in
4. The problem never happens on 4.1.7 or earlier version

### Expected behaviour

It should not be stuck and when you click log in you will be able to see the login page with a single button log in with the OAuth

### Actual behaviour

It will stuck on the page

### Detailed description

_No response_

### Mastodon instance

mfy.social

### Mastodon version

v4.2.0 Nightly

### Browser name and version

Edge Latest

### Operating system

macOS 13.5.1

### Technical details

https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/81caafbe84240bfb730f5001b33add97ebcbe9dc/spec/requests/content_security_policy_spec.rb#L20

I checked the detailed log and browser's console log, seems like this line is causing the problem? I am just guessing
comments: What do you mean by “you stuck on the page you are in”? Can you provide more details? Which part of the flow is it stuck on? What's in the browser's console log?

Hi @ClearlyClaire , thank you for the reply and let me give you more details:
1. The page I am in means that: I set the env without OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true firstly and Mastodon worked fine. I logged in and view some pages and all are functional.
2. After I added OMNIAUTH_ONLY=true to the env and recreate the container, this problem will happen, I cannot neither log in nor log out
![image](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/assets/53750381/9d6ff69e-2a85-4d78-b717-b70a72addd19)
The log in button will become like this:
![image](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/assets/53750381/8a1134ef-a941-459a-abce-7b341c223543)
And when I click the button I will get this error in browser's console log 
![image](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/assets/53750381/8413c799-5ade-494f-b167-6db610866056)
```
Refused to send form data to 'https://mastodondomain/auth/auth/openid_connect' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "form-action 'self'".
```

This problem only happens in the nightly image for version 4.2.0, I tried to do the same thing and use the latest tag for the image which is the version 4.1.7, it works fine without any issues. So this is weird. As https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/81caafbe84240bfb730f5001b33add97ebcbe9dc/spec/requests/content_security_policy_spec.rb#L20 This commit was done two month ago, which should influence both the version. I am not familiar with Mastodon's source code, this is just my guess

> `Refused to send form data to 'https://mastodondomain/auth/auth/openid_connect' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "form-action 'self'".`

Is that a *different* domain? It sounds like it shouldn't be.

`form-action 'self'` is involved, yes, but it's only part of the issue; there was an interstitial page before #26083
It is the same domain for sure, which is mfy.social same as the main domain

> form-action 'self' is involved, yes, but it's only part of the issue; there was an interstitial page before https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/26083

Yeah you are right, this issue must have something related to this PR

oh, right, this does a `POST` to `https://mfy.social/auth/auth/openid_connect` which is a fine first step, but then that page does a 302 to an external domain, which is allowed by certain browsers and blocked by other browsers

cc @CSDUMMI

Sorry, I forgot to include this in the PR I made introducing the single-step login with 'OMINAUTH_ONLY=true'. 

The way I solved this before was by adding another env variable `SSO_HOST` with the domain of the SSO provider used and adding that domain to the `form-action` CSP.

But I think a better solution would be to extract the domain from the configuration variable used, such as `OIDC_ISSUER`.

I can make a PR with a bug fix for that.
@ClearlyClaire @CSDUMMI Thank you so much for confirming this!

review_comments:
I believe this should be:
```suggestion
    ENV['OIDC_AUTH_ENDPOINT'] || OpenIDConnect::Discovery::Provider::Config.discover!(ENV['OIDC_ISSUER']).authorization_endpoint if ENV['OIDC_ENABLED'] == 'true'
```
